To test the impacts of an “off” mode of the AMOC on the Tibetan Plateau during deglaciations, we first conducted an equilibrated glacial control simulation (GCTL) by imposing the fixed boundary conditions of the Last Glacial Maximum as proposed by the PMIP3 protocol.

GCTL is integrated for 3000 years to an equilibrated state that serves as a basis for a classic North Atlantic (NA) hosing experiment (GFWF) in which a freshwater flux of 0.2 Sv (1 Sv = 10 6 m 3 /s) was imposed into the Ice-Rafted Debris Belt for 800 years to shut down deep-water formation in the North Atlantic.
In this study, GFWF is not aimed at reproducing HS1 as in previous studies but rather mimicking a generic deglacial Heinrich event with an “off” mode of the AMOC.
